MAYOR’S FUND SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES
  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

Leanna Noble, Member  Stephen Wood, Member
Angela Russell, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Health Department staff Jennifer Santana called the meeting to order at 3:15 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Noble, Russell

  Commissioners Absent: Wood

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Joseph Botelho, Community
Program Specialist V, Jennifer Santana, Community Program Specialist.

Roll call was taken by Jennifer Santana.
  • For the record member Stephen Wood was absent and unexcused.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-55969  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Mayor’s
  Fund Subcommittee meeting of Monday, June 8, 2026.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  2  Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Wood

2.  26-56208  Recommendation to receive and file the Mayor’s Fund Balance Update from the
  Health Department

  • Health department staff Jennifer Santana provided the Mayor’s Fund
  balance and contributions for the month of August 2026. As of September
  2026 there is one outstanding MOU.

3.  26-55970  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, approve the Mayor’s Fund
  Subcommittee grant application submitted by Christian Outreach in Action for
  funding in the amount of $30,000.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion failed by the following vote:

  Yes:  0  None
  No:  2  Noble, Russell
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Wood

  • Health department staff provided an overview of the grant application and
  shared concerns regarding the application. The meeting was paused for a
  moment as quorum was lost.
  • Subcommittee members have similiar concerns as staff, the applicant does
  not believe that the application meets the intent of the Mayor’s Fund.
  • The members moved to not recommend the application for further
  consideration.

4.  26-55971  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, approve the Mayor’s Fund
  Subcommittee grant application submitted by Long Beach New Life Fellowship for
  funding in the amount of $5,000.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion failed by the following vote:

  Yes:  0  None
  No:  2  Noble, Russell
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Wood

  • Health department staff shared an overview along with the cost breakdown
  for this application. No members from the organization were present at the

  meeting.
  • Staff shared concerns regarding the hot meal program, the need for this
  service is needed and appreciated, however not aligned with the intent of the
  Mayor’s Fund.
  • The members moved to not recommend the application for further
  consideration.

5.  26-55972  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, approve the Mayor’s Fund
  Subcommittee grant application submitted by Prep ED Programs Inc. for funding in
  the amount of $10,000.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  2  Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Wood

  • Applicant Claude Diles III provided background information regarding the
  organization and the work it performs. The subcommittee followed up with
  additional questions regarding the application. Health Department staff noted
  that they would not weigh heavily on the application due to a potential dual
  relationship, as the applicant currently serves on the Long Beach Continuum
  of Care Board. Staff noted that, based on the initial threshold review, the
  application aligns with the intent of the Mayor’s Fund.
  • The subcommittee moved to approve the application in the amount of
  $10,000.
  • A member of the public provided comments regarding the collaboration
  between Prep Ed Programs Inc. and Transformational Living Homes and the
  success they have had in supporting clients.

6.  26-55973  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, approve the Mayor’s Fund
  Subcommittee grant application submitted by RT Care Relief Corp for funding in
  the amount of $10,000.

  A Laid Over was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, Laid
  Over. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  2  Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None

  Page 3 of 5
   MAYOR’S FUND SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES
  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

  Absent:  1 Wood

  • Health Department staff provided a brief summary of the application and the
  requested award amount. Staff expressed concerns regarding the
  organization’s work, noting that the City is not sufficiently familiar with the
  organization to fully assess the validity and potential impact of its services in
  Long Beach.
  • The subcommittee requested to table the item to allow the organization an
  opportunity to provide additional information regarding the work it conducts in
  Long Beach, any partnerships or collaborations with the City, and supporting
  information demonstrating the validity and impact of its work.

7.  26-55974  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, approve the Mayor’s Fund
  Subcommittee grant application submitted by Transformational Living Homes for
  funding in the amount of $9,862.50.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  2  Noble, Russell
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Wood

  • A representative from Transformational Living Homes provided the
  subcommittee and staff with a brief overview of the organization’s work in the
  Long Beach community, including providing bed nights for individuals
  experiencing homelessness. The organization indicated that it would use the
  requested funding to establish a formalized pilot program and encourage
  additional funders and partnerships to support the program.
  • Staff stated that the application meets the intent of the Mayor’s Fund and
  addresses a gap in services. Staff noted that the organization assists
  individuals experiencing homelessness in transitioning to stable housing by
  providing interim and ongoing shared-living resources at a cost-effective
  rate. The organization partners with several service providers, and staff have
  visited its sites and reported no concerns.
  • A member of the public who previously participated in Transformational
  Living Homes’ housing program shared their personal experience and
  described their success as a result of participating in the program.
  • A member of the public provided comments regarding Transformational
  Living Homes’ work and its collaborations with other organizations.

8.  26-56209  Recommendation to discuss and, if appropriate, approve the Mayor’s Fund

   MAYOR’S FUND SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES
  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

  Subcommittee grant application submitted by Long Beach Grace Samoan Church
  of the Nazarene for funding in the amount of $10,000

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Russell, to
  approve recommendation. The motion failed by the following vote:

  Yes:  0  None
  No:  2  Noble, Russell
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Wood

  • Health Department staff provided an overview of the application and shared
  concerns regarding the proposed use of funds. Staff stated that, while
  providing Thanksgiving hot meals addresses an important community need,
  the proposed activity does not align with the intent of the Mayor’s Fund.
  • The subcommittee shared the concerns and moved to not recommend the
  application to move forward.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Subcommittee members expressed interest in encouraging additional HSAC members to join
  the subcommittee. Staff shared that the number of applications received this month was higher
  than in previous years.

ADJOURNMENT

Clerk Jennifer Santana adjourned the meeting at 4:12 p.m.
